question:
A recurring workflow in our team passes work from one person to the next, and today only two senior developers know how it goes. I want to write it down so that new developers and automated coding agents follow it the same way every time: what must the write-up state, and in what forms can it be written?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

Document recurring workflows so both humans and automated agents can follow them consistently. Write-ups must specify required inputs, transforming activities, outputs, controls, and enabling mechanisms. Multiple notation forms are acceptable, from natural language to formal diagrams. Clear roles, responsibilities, and rationale for decisions must be included.

# Guidelines

- A process write-up must describe [SWEBOK excerpt 220f7360a1a611bdbd6b]; it may also [SWEBOK excerpt c71f5dd4727992c59cd3]). (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Software Engineering Processes and System Lifecycles/Software Engineering Process Definition and Structure/Software Process Definition and Components.md)

- The write-up must make clear that [SWEBOK excerpt 24f5a67c87fc0b0f7a43], capturing the hand-off points explicitly. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Software Engineering Processes and System Lifecycles/Software Engineering Process Definition and Structure/Software Process Definition and Components.md)

- The write-up can be expressed in any of several accepted notations, including natural language, textual lists of [SWEBOK excerpt 06a1aefa5cbd17610943], IDEF0, Petri nets, UML activity diagrams, or BPMN. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Software Process Foundations and Measurement/Software Process Infrastructure Tools and Notations.md)

- The specification must [SWEBOK excerpt ccb8650d8904cabfb53a], and must be easy to understand and correct, since it will serve as the basis for coordination, measurement, assessment, and quality management. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Software Processes and Life Cycle Management/Software Process Definition and Life Cycle Specification.md)

- The write-up must specify inputs and outputs for each step, and must reflect that inputs to one process are very often outputs from other processes, capturing those inter-process dependencies. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Software Processes and Life Cycle Management/Software Process Definition and Life Cycle Specification.md)

- Roles and responsibilities must be stated clearly enough [SWEBOK excerpt c36779fd1df611867044]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/ISO 9001 and Software Quality Assurance Management Systems.md)

- Procedures must [SWEBOK excerpt c284d7a5887b0100847a], with the user of the document in mind, and must identify where quality controls are to be verified. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Quality Management Systems and Process Evaluation/Software Quality Management System Implementation and Evaluation.md)

- The write-up must be accessible, understandable, and relevant to its intended audience, including new developers and automated coding agents. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Collaboration, Communication, and Cognition in Software Engineering/Writing and Communication in Software Engineering.md)

- The write-up should record the rationale for each nontrivial decision, including [SWEBOK excerpt c828a4ed83fe16794b0b] analyzed, to support those who modify or maintain the workflow after deployment. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Design Concerns, Documentation, and Modeling/Recording Design Rationale for System Maintainability.md)

- Everything described in the workflow write-up should be [SWEBOK excerpt b9e343c38a04177e69e8] — or agent — could replicate the results. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Test Generation, Environment Setup, and Incident Management/Test Environment Setup and Controlled Experimentation.md)

- Repetitive steps in the workflow should be noted as candidates for automation using scripting, [SWEBOK excerpt 46c430e4b294282a47c2]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Installation and Operational Verification Processes/Software Deployment and Automation/Scripting and Automating Operational Tasks.md)

- The write-up must document relevant facts, significant risks and trade-offs, and problems encountered, and must [SWEBOK excerpt 79de000b38ddc0c159e4] workflow remains in use. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)

- The workflow documentation should capture domain knowledge, programming practices, and organisation and presentation issues to reduce the comprehension effort required by software engineers who did not originally design the workflow. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Maintenance_ Technical, Management, and Comprehension Challenges/Limited Understanding in Software Maintenance.md)

- Requirements or steps within the write-up may use structured natural language formats such as actor-action format, user story format, or use-case specification templates to increase precision and conciseness. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Requirements_ Foundations and Engineering Practices/Requirements Engineering_ Elicitation, Analysis, and Specification/Requirements Specification and Validation Techniques/Requirement Specification Formats and Structures/Actor-Action Format in Requirements Statements.md)

- A handoff process between the people passing work must be explicitly defined within the write-up, with quality documentation maintained on all tasks and changes regardless of team structure. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Maintenance Management and Organization/Organizing Software Maintenance Responsibilities/Developer vs. Separate Maintenance Team Trade-offs.md)
